description: Watch ops — spawn background pollers for external sources (MRs, jobs, calendar) that emit events via UDS socket + status files + macOS notifications. Reusable foundation; channel consumer plugs in later.

watch.description: Spawn a background poller for SOURCE:ID. Optional :only=ev1,ev2 filters which events emit notifications. PID file: /tmp/supertool-watch-{SOURCE}__{ID}.pid

unwatch.description: Stop every live poller for SOURCE:ID and remove its PID file. A slot can hold more than one poller, so this is a multi-kill: the tracked PID plus any poller whose own argv names this exact source and id. Every PID is printed with its provenance (tracked/untracked) before anything is signalled, one that cannot be stopped is named rather than swallowed (exit 1), and an absence is only reported as an absence when the process scan actually ran — 'no PID file', 'tracked PID is dead', and 'could not check' are three different answers. A poller spawned before the argv labelling landed wears its parent's command line and cannot be reached; those need `pkill -f presets/watch/` once.

watches.description: List active watch pollers as a table: source, id, pid, started, last_event. Built from PID files AND a scan for labelled poller processes, so it also shows what the PID files alone cannot: an id running more than one poller (count plus every PID), and a poller whose PID file was deleted ('no pidfile'). This is the authoritative view of the fleet — `ps` output cannot identify a watcher, because a poller spawned before the argv labelling wears the argv of whatever forked it.

channel.description: Whether the watch -> Claude-session bridge is actually delivering (#554). `pgrep channel.ts`, `lsof` on the socket and writing to it are all green whether events arrive or not, so this asks a different question and answers it in three states, never two. NOT DELIVERING (exit 1) is a definite negative — nothing is listening, so every event a poller emits right now is lost at the source, and the report names the watchers that already were. FORWARDING (exit 0) reads the consumer's own published counters: lines read, forwarded, dropped, last forwarded, refreshed on a 10s heartbeat so an idle consumer and a wedged one are distinguishable. CANNOT DETERMINE (exit 3) is everything else — bound but publishing no counters, counters written by a pid that is gone, counters gone stale — and it is the state today's tooling reports as green. It now names the process holding the socket, so `nothing is consuming this` and `another session is consuming this` stop rendering identically: `socket-holder: pid N — not this process`, or the refusal the probe returned, never a bare verdict. `forwarded` means handed to the MCP transport and never means delivered: the bridge sends a JSON-RPC notification, which has no response to wait on, so whether an event reached a session is observable only from inside that session. Honours SUPERTOOL_WATCH_NAME, which derives both the socket and the poller state directory from one word; SUPERTOOL_WATCH_SOCK and SUPERTOOL_WATCH_STATE_DIR still override it and the report prints the override. Set the same name in the claude-channel `env` block of .mcp.json — nothing in .supertool.json reaches the consumer, and this op reads that file and reports a disagreement rather than assuming agreement. Branch on the report's first line (`channel: FORWARDING|NOT DELIVERING|CANNOT DETERMINE`) rather than on the exit code: the distinct codes 0/1/3 survive only when presets/watch/channel.py is run directly, because the supertool wrapper collapses every non-zero to 1.

radar.description: Reconcile registered radar tiers against live truth, then report. Tiers are registered in ops.radar.radar_tiers (reaches the preset as SUPERTOOL_RADAR_TIERS) and there is no default: with none configured radar refuses and names the fix, because an unconfigured radar that prints nothing is byte-identical to a healthy one. `{"gl-mrs": {}}` is the GitLab MR board — live MRs are authoritative, state files are cache; it prunes terminal state files, flags pipeline drift (last_event vs source_state), respawns watchers for open MRs with no live poller, and keeps one gitlab-mr-feed poller alive so MRs opened after this run are still discovered. `{"gl-runners": {}}` adds the runner fleet. Full board on cold start, delta-only after. Idempotent — safe on every session start. Takes the gl-mrs filter vocabulary; the board, the watcher fleet and the feed are always one resolved filter. Standing exclusions live in ops.radar.radar_exclusions. {'gh-prs': {}} is the GitHub PR board — same reconcile, one `gh pr list` call, plus the default branch as a board member (the red-master case no PR covers). It refuses a filter token it cannot honour instead of running the query without it, counts a PR with no check rollup as unchecked rather than green, keys its delta on the head SHA, and reports watch coverage as UNKNOWN under a repo target because watch state is keyed by PR number alone. There is no GitHub discovery feed, so new PRs are found on the next tick and the footer says so. `radar:--state` is the read-only view: which module each registered name resolved to, the options it accepted, the ones it did not recognise, and — for a tier exposing radar_state() — its resolved scope, snapshot file and live pollers. It spawns nothing, reaps nothing and calls no API, so it is safe when you only want to look, while a bare radar heals and forks pollers. It is an argument rather than its own op because ops.radar.radar_tiers merges into the op it is keyed by, so a second op name would need a second copy of the tier list — and a read-only view describing a different tier set from the one radar runs is the very defect it exists to remove.
